item.title: Canada July trade surplus shrinks, U.S. exports drop
item.description: Canada’s trade surplus sharply narrowed in July as exports of energy and metal products shrank while imports rose, data showed on Thursday, just weeks before a major escalation in trade dispute with ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — Canada’s trade surplus narrowed sharply in July as exports of energy and metal products shrank while imports rose, just weeks before Washington’s new 50 per cent tariffs begin to show up in statistics, posing a stiffer test for Canadian exporters. The trade surplus was $769 million, compared with a four-year high surplus of $4.2 billion posted a month ago, Statistics Canada said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a surplus of $3.57 billion in July. Exports dropped 2.3 per cent, while imports increased 2.2 per cent. Amid an escalating trade dispute with U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration, Canada has been seeking to reduce its dependence on its neighbor and largest trading partner. The U.S. accounted for 66.35 per cent of Canada’s total exports in July, down from 69.39 per cent in June and 72.64 per cent a year ago. However, Canada’s import dependence on the U.S. has only narrowed to 59 per cent in the last 12 months compared with 62 per cent in 2024. The July figures, Canada’s fifth consecutive monthly trade surplus, extended a run of relatively resilient Canadian trade despite more than a year and a half of U.S. tariffs. However, Washington’s latest duties, imposed last month, will provide a tougher test for exporters in the coming months. The decrease in exports in July was primarily led by energy products, which account for almost a quarter of Canada’s total exports, and 95 per cent of which usually flow south of the border. Their value dropped 4.4 per cent in July, a third consecutive monthly decline after exports of crude oil decreased by 5.5 per cent, with both prices and volumes falling, StatsCan said. Exports of metal and non-metallic mineral products, which posted an increase of 15.8 per cent in the prior month, also shrank by 8.5 per cent in July. As a result, Canada’s total exports fell to $76.14 billion, down from $77.96 billion in June, but excluding metals and energy, exports increased 0.6 per cent in July. The overall decrease in total exports in July was partially offset by higher exports of aircraft and other transportation equipment and parts, which surged by 34.9 per cent. Imports rose in July to a value of $75.37 billion, up from $73.76 billion, StatsCan said, adding that it was the sixth consecutive monthly increase. This was led by an 11.4 per cent increase in imports of motor vehicles and parts, mainly from the U.S. Exports to the U.S. dropped 6.6 per cent in July while imports from the country increased by 1.8 per cent, shrinking Canada’s trade surplus with its main trading partner by more than 40 per cent to $5.9 billion. Stuart Bergman, chief economist at Export Development Canada, the country’s official export credit agency, said that keeping the share of Canada’s exports going to the U.S. below 70 per cent was an encouraging trend. “Sheer gravity alone pulls exporters to the U.S. market,” Bergman said, but added that there have been concerted efforts to shift some of that gravity to other markets, citing the increase in agricultural exports, especially canola to China and Japan. Year-to-date share of exports to the U.S. is around 68 per cent, down from 73 per cent in the year-ago period. Exports to countries other than the United States rose 7.4 per cent, while imports increased 2.8 per cent, leaving Canada with a non-U.S. trade deficit of $5.1 billion, down from $6.1 billion in the prior month. The Canadian dollar was trading firmer, up 0.35 per cent to $1.3792 against the U.S. dollar, or 72.51 U.S. cents. --- Reporting by Promit Mukherjee; Editing by Dale Smith; Editing by Sharon Singleton

item.title: Air Canada targets global growth with new routes, while U.S. travel demand still sags
item.description: Air Canada is embarking on a major expansion of its overseas network, announcing seven new routes in Europe and Asia.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: MONTREAL — Air Canada has embarked on a major expansion of its network overseas, announcing seven new routes in Europe and Asia for next summer. Chief commercial officer Mark Galardo says the move signals a push to become a fully international carrier as the country’s largest airline aims to draw more on higher-margin globetrotters and less on purely domestic customers. “We talked about an Air Canada that would be further transforming itself into a global airline — not just a Canadian airline, a true global airline — and be focusing on further building its long-haul network,” Galardo said in a phone interview. The build-out also comes as Air Canada and its competitors struggle to navigate fuel costs as the Iran war drags on, a prolonged plunge in Canadian demand for U.S. travel and the years-long closure of Russian airspace to Western airlines — a serious hurdle to travel between North America and Asia, given the polar routes through Siberian skies. To help offset those challenges, the airline plans to launch new service to five foreign cities including Guangzhou, China — the trip from Vancouver steers clear of Russia — Oslo, Norway, and Dubrovnik, Croatia, cementing its status as the second-largest North American airline by overseas destinations served. Galardo stressed Canada’s location as ideal for layovers on trips between the Americas and Europe, which make up a key source of revenue. “What’s really critical for us is to position Canada as a global transit point for traffic to and from the Americas at large,” he said, pointing to Air Canada’s biggest hubs in Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver. “We’re 42 million Canadians, but when you look at our geographic placement, we can effectively serve a market that’s a billion people wide and deep.” Driving the expansion are new long-range Airbus A321 single-aisle jets as well as Boeing 787 wide-bodies, though major delivery delays have hampered their rollout. The first of an expected 30 A321XLRs arrived at Air Canada in April, with a “big batch” en route in 2027 and the final delivery slated for 2029, Galardo said. The Montreal-based company scaled back an initial order of 18 787-10s to 14 of the Boeing jets last fall amid production delays, but the first is set to touch down later this year and enter service in 2027. “Better late than never,” Galardo said. By next summer, Air Canada aims to operate more than 125 international routes to 85-plus destinations, excluding the U.S. The expansion will mark an eight per cent jump in overseas flight volumes compared to the summer of 2026. --- Christopher Reynolds, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 3, 2026.

item.description: Oracle is scheduled to release its Q1 FY2027 earnings on September 9, 2026. Oracle displays solid profitability and high ROE driven by cloud service expansion, but it maintains significant leverage ...
item.content:encoded:
Kim Bolton, President and Portfolio Manager, Black Swan Dexteritas Focus: Technology stocks

Top Picks: Cadence Design Systems , Shopify , Oracle MARKET OUTLOOK: The market chatters these days, is about September, traditionally the weakest month of the year for stocks, but remember the last two Septembers were positive. All in, the S&P 500’s average September performance since 1945 has been a decline of 0.7 per cent. Even worse, Septembers in midterm years have tended to be even weaker, with the S&P 500 averaging a decline of 1.3 per cent, or nearly twice the decline of all years. With this background, now is the time for risk management to be vigilant. While the market searches for the next fundamental catalyst, technical signal, and changes in capital flows, your Black Swan Dexteritas (BSD) team will continue to trim those securities that are achieving their respective intrinsic values, and buy those technology growth stocks that exhibit longer, more lucrative investment runways. The hedging overlay continues to be an important tool to protect your capital in bearish markets, and an important tool to be ‘dialed down’ in bullish markets. Within the technology arena the software sector has been in the doghouse. However, the emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) enterprise software is moving from AI systems that generate answers to AI systems that can plan, coordinate, make decisions, use tools, and execute work across applications. The key investor question is shifting from who has the best chatbot? to which platforms are becoming the operating layer through which autonomous digital work is executed. Your BSD Team is proud to be your investment ‘eyes and ears’ in the technology arena. Market-moving news, fast:  Get the BNN Bloomberg App now Sign up for the Market Call Top Picks newsletter at  bnnbloomberg.ca/newsletters TOP PICKS: Kim Bolton's Top Picks: Cadence Design Systems, Shopify & Oracle Kim Bolton, president and portfolio manager at Black Swan Dexteritas, shares his top stock picks to watch in the market.

Cadence Design Systems (CDNS NASDAQ) Cadence Design Systems, Inc. is an American multinational computational software company that provides electronic design automation (EDA) software, hardware, and intellectual property (IP) for designing integrated circuits, systems-on-chips, and printed circuit boards. Cadence Design Systems demonstrates strong financial health backed by robust profitability, high gross margins, and healthy liquidity metrics. While valuation ratios like price–earnings ratio (P/E) reflect a significant market premium due to high demand for AI-driven Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software, recent strategic acquisitions have introduced moderate debt, which remains well-managed against strong operating cash flows." 30 Days performance: -9.20 per cent 100 Days performance: -20.04 per cent Buy one-third of a position here at approximately US$305.24 add at approximately US$289.98 and approximately US$274.72 Shopify (SHOP NASDAQ) Shopify Inc. is a Canadian multinational e-commerce company that provides a cloud-based software-as-a-service platform for online stores and retail point-of-sale systems. Deepened strategic collaboration with AWS to expand Oracle AI Database availability to 22 regions. Introduced new AI agents and Fusion Agentic Applications to enhance talent management and supply chain operations. Partnered with Quantinuum to accelerate hybrid quantum compute adoption on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Announced availability of Oracle Health’s AI-powered patient portal. Oracle is scheduled to release its Q1 FY2027 earnings on September 9, 2026.
